title: North Central Airlines 458
summary: During a night approach to O'Hare in 200-foot ceilings and light rain, at 210 feet the CV-580 began climbing. The captain initiated a go-around but the aircraft continued climbing and stalled. It rolled left, struck the ground, and crashed into a hangar. The NTSB determined the captain experienced spatial disorientation from atmospheric refraction of approach lights at a critical moment when transitioning between instrument and visual reference.
probable_cause: Spatial disorientation of the captain caused by atmospheric refraction of approach lights during transition from instrument to visual flight reference, combined with relatively low command experience in the CV-580.

factors.evidence: The aircraft began its approach to O'Hare, which had a 200 ft ceiling with light rain and fog
Spatial disorientation of the captain precipitated by atmospheric refraction of either the approach lights or landing lights at a critical point in the approach
the captain of Flight 458, although experienced, had relatively few hours of experience as the pilot-in-command in CV-580s
Flight 458 lost speed until it stalled 13 seconds after the initiation of the go-around
The aircraft entered a steep left bank, and its left wing struck the ground

events.text: Aircraft at 20:14 CST began approach to O'Hare with 200 ft ceiling, light rain and fog
Flight cleared to descend to 3,500 ft, RVR reported as 4,500 feet
Flight instructed to slow to 160 knots, vectored for ILS approach to Runway 14R
Flight vectored left to 050° then right to 090° for spacing
Flight instructed to turn right to 220° and maintain until ILS localizer interception
Flight reported at outer marker (Romeo), cleared for ILS approach, new RVR 2,600 feet
Aircraft at approximately 210 feet above airport elevation, about 4,500 feet from runway threshold, descended normally on ILS glideslope
Aircraft entered unexpected sustained climb of approximately 1,244 feet per minute
Captain called for full available power (971 rpm or 4,000 hp) and initiated go-around procedures
Aircraft continued climbing despite go-around attempt, gaining additional 500 feet to 940 feet altitude, airspeed decreased to point where aerodynamic control was lost
Aircraft stalled 13 seconds after go-around initiation, entered steep left bank, left wing struck ground
Aircraft impacted main door of hangar in near-inverted position approximately 100 feet southeast of runway threshold, destroyed by impact and fire

notes: Read: synopsis, probable cause, findings, recommendations

recommendations.text: Section 121.652 of the Federal Aviation Regulations be amended to prohibit a captain from being removed from "high" minimums until he has accrued 100 hours as pilot-in-command in type
